judged_text: The guests array has no maxItems bound and each invocation emails every existing attendee plus every team member, so request cost is unbounded in input size and grows with the attendee list. A single request can create thousands of Attendee rows and fan out thousands of emails plus calendar API calls inside one mutation; adding guests one at a time to a large booking resends the full attendee/team email set per invocation, an O(N²) email pattern operators will see as slow requests and mail-provider rate limits.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows unbounded input and fan-out work: ZAddGuestsInputSchema allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no max, and `addGuestsHandler` does `attendees.createMany` for all `uniqueGuests` (no cap). It then builds `evt.attendees` from *all* booking attendees (`bookingAttendees.attendees.map(...)`) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` plus `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, where `sendAddGuestsEmails` emails the organizer, each team member, and then maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` to send an email per attendee. This means each invocation’s cost grows with current attendee list, and repeated “add guests” calls will repeatedly email the full attendee set (quadratic total over many invocations). This is a concrete, diff-grounded scalability/operational-risk concern rather than a clearly incorrect behavior.
